comparison: Perfect agreement on model comparison claims (C4, C42-C43, C99, C133). Both evaluations find strong support that active inference outperformed reinforcement learning models. OpenEval notes lack of effect sizes/confidence intervals, while peer reviewers explicitly affirmed the finding without raising this concern.

Both support the main conclusion (C139) that active inference accounts for human decision-making under uncertainty. OpenEval is more cautious, noting limitations (small sample, model fit issues, multiple comparison concerns) and calling it 'preliminary support.' Peer reviewers provide stronger endorsement, calling evidence 'solid' and study 'compelling and comprehensive.'

Both support behavioral findings (C44-C52). OpenEval notes lack of explicit statistical tests and effect sizes. Peer reviewers accepted behavioral patterns without challenge, viewing them as consistent with active inference predictions. OpenEval also includes C92 on exploration variance that peer reviewers address separately.

Both support sensor-level EEG findings (C5, C56-C57, C112). OpenEval raises concerns about lack of multiple comparison correction and speculative interpretation of encoding environmental structure. Peer reviewers accepted findings without these concerns, noting regions are 'illuminating and useful as candidate regions.'

Both support sensor-level findings (C6, C60-C61, C63). OpenEval notes concerns about multiple comparison corrections and speculative interpretation of hidden state encoding. Peer reviewers accepted these findings as part of the overall sensor-level results without specific concerns about interpretation.

Divergent evaluations of source-level findings (C7, C64-C65, C134). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes concerns about FDR correction and use of average head model. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly cautioning that 'regions showing up as correlated with model parameters change depending on source modelling method and correction for multiple comparisons.'

Divergent evaluations of uncertainty encoding claims (C8, C66-C67, C72-C73, C76-C77, C82, C135-C136). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with caveats about multiple comparisons. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, expressing caution about source localization reliability and noting authors' own acknowledgment (C132) that only subset of regions survive correction.

Divergent evaluations of source-level findings (C74-C75, C78-C81). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED despite concerns about multiple comparisons. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, expressing general caution about all source localization findings due to methodological sensitivity.

Divergent evaluations of temporal/functional distinctions (C70-C71, C128-C129). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing findings as supporting active inference framework. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN as part of broader caution about source-level claims.

Both express uncertainty about result stage findings (C83-C85). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN citing authors' acknowledgment of unreliability. Peer reviewers' UNCERTAIN rating for source localization generally encompasses these claims.

Divergent evaluations of functional interpretations (C118-C124). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with caveats about reverse inference limitations. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN as part of broader caution about source localization, though R9 separately supports the literature contextualization aspect.

Both support literature integration (C119-C120, C122-C123). OpenEval notes these are functional interpretations with reverse inference limitations. Peer reviewers accepted the literature contextualization as 'sensible' without challenging the appropriateness of citations.

Divergent evaluations of overlapping uncertainty representations (C125-C127). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with caveats about tentative language and unreliable Second result stage. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN as part of general caution about source localization findings.

Both acknowledge multiple comparison issues (C132). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for honest reporting but notes it undermines confidence in source-level findings. Peer reviewers cite this same limitation as reason for UNCERTAIN rating on source localization claims.

Both support simulation results (C33-C40). OpenEval notes these are computational demonstrations rather than empirical findings about human behavior. Peer reviewers praised the 'cleverly designed' paradigm without distinguishing simulation from empirical components.

Both support methodological details (C26, C31-C32, C41). OpenEval provides comprehensive assessment including sample size concerns. Peer reviewers praised experimental design as 'cleverly designed' and 'elegant' without raising sample size concerns.

Divergent evaluations of methods (C3, C159-C162). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with note about small sample size. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, raising specific concern about 1 Hz high-pass filter potentially removing sustained/slow processes related to active inference quantities.

Divergent evaluations of EEG preprocessing (C163-C170). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting methods follow established practices with acknowledged limitation of average head model. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, specifically concerned that 1 Hz filter may miss relevant slow processes, though noting this represents a tradeoff rather than a flaw.

Both support learning trajectory interpretations (C55, C58, C108-C109). OpenEval notes these involve inference about unmeasured internal states. Peer reviewers accepted interpretations as 'sensible' without challenging the inferential nature.

Both support information availability interpretations (C59, C62, C110-C111). OpenEval notes speculative elements and unvalidated assumptions about neural-confidence relationships. Peer reviewers accepted without challenge as part of overall 'sensible' discussion.

Both support acknowledgment of model limitations (C53-C54, C130-C131). OpenEval views as honest self-assessment with untested hypotheses. Peer reviewers accepted limitations without additional concern.

Both support explanation of novelty discrepancy (C113-C117). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting good scientific practice but speculative explanation. Peer reviewers accepted without challenge as part of overall interpretation.
Both support literature comparison (C114, C116-C117). OpenEval emphasizes speculative nature of explanation. Peer reviewers accepted as appropriate contextualization within existing literature.

Both support theoretical framework (C1-C2, C9-C12, C27-C30, C97, C140-C158). OpenEval notes these are established principles not tested in this study. Peer reviewers accepted as appropriate background, noting introduction makes findings 'accessible to a broad readership.'

Both support exploration strategy theory (C86-C96). OpenEval notes theoretical claims well-supported by citations, with C92 behavioral finding lacking quantitative variance measures. Peer reviewers accepted theoretical framework without challenge.
Both support high variance in exploration strategies (C92). OpenEval notes lack of specific quantitative measures. Peer reviewers accepted as part of behavioral evidence for active inference.

Both support discussion of active inference strengths/limitations (C98-C107). OpenEval notes balanced treatment with concern about falsifiability from complete class theorem. Peer reviewers accepted theoretical discussion without raising falsifiability concerns.

Both support literature review establishing research gap (C13-C25). OpenEval notes claims accurately characterize field and motivate study design. Peer reviewers accepted as addressing 'fundamental distinction' and 'central question in systems neuroscience.'
Both support model fit limitations (C53). OpenEval views as honest acknowledgment of untested hypotheses. Peer reviewers accepted without additional concern as part of behavioral evidence.
